question: The generation of heat in a conductor due to electric current is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule’s heating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joule’s heating**, also known as **ohmic heating** or **resistive heating**, occurs when an electric current passes through a conductor, producing heat due to the resistance of the material.
 
• The heat generated in the conductor is governed by **Joule’s Law**, which states that the heat produced is directly proportional to the square of the current (*I*), the resistance (*R*), and the time (*t*) for which the current flows: *H = I²Rt*.
 
• Joule’s heating effect is utilized in various devices such as **electric heaters**, **toasters**, **electric kettles**, and **incandescent bulbs**.
 
• The phenomenon is a result of collisions between electrons (carrying current) and the lattice ions in the conductor, which convert the electrical energy into thermal energy.
 
• This effect is not ideal for transmission of electricity over long distances as it leads to **energy loss** in the form of heat, thus necessitating efficient electrical systems to minimize Joule’s heating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrolysis:**

 
 
• Electrolysis is a chemical process where **electric current causes the decomposition** of a compound in a liquid solution or molten state, typically used in the extraction or purification of metals.
 
• An example is the **electrolysis of water**, which splits water molecules into **hydrogen** and **oxygen gases**.
 
• It is fundamentally different from Joule’s heating as it involves chemical changes rather than heat generation.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law:**
 
 
• Ohm’s Law defines the relationship between voltage (*V*), current (*I*), and resistance (*R*) in an electrical circuit: *V = IR*.
 
• It does not directly explain the generation of heat, but it helps in calculating the current or resistance, which can then be used in **Joule’s heating formula**.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when an electric current is generated in a conductor due to a changing magnetic field.
 
• It is the principle behind devices like **generators** and **transformers** and does not involve the generation of heat like Joule’s heating.
 
• Discovered by **Michael Faraday** in **1831**, electromagnetic induction is central to modern power generation systems.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Joule’s Heating:**
 
 
• It is widely used in heating devices such as **electric irons**, **room heaters**, and **electric stoves**.
 
• It plays a role in the functioning of **fuses**, where excessive current causes heating and breaks the circuit.
 
• Joule’s heating is also utilized in **thermistors** and **temperature-dependent resistors** for various applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Loss in Transmission:**

 
 
• Joule’s heating leads to significant **energy loss** during the transmission of electricity over long distances, which is why **high voltage transmission** is preferred to minimize current and reduce losses.
 
 
 
• **Practical Limitations:**
 
 
• Excessive Joule’s heating can damage electrical components and circuits, necessitating the use of **cooling systems** and **efficient designs**.
 
 
 
• **Discovery:**
 
 
• Joule’s heating was first described by **James Prescott Joule** in the **1840s**, laying the foundation for thermodynamics and modern electrical engineering.
